$comment: One entry per method: its body, or one body per request op (`selected_by`). `encoding` is the ResultPayload variant; a `Raw` body is a MessagePack `bin` holding the MessagePack encoding of `schema`, a `Json` body is that value as a JSON tree. A body with a `dynamic` reason is chosen by the caller and has the unconstrained schema `true`.

AccessDecision.description:
`CheckAccess`'s answer: would `agent_id`'s request of `access` on `graph`
be admitted right now, by the same isolation/RBAC decision EG applies to
that principal's own requests. An unregistered or revoked principal is
`allowed: false`.

roles.description:
RBAC role names this agent holds (CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature). Expanded transitively
through the role hierarchy by the policy evaluator. The field is mandatory in
every current wire and durable identity image; an omitted authorization claim
is rejected during deserialization instead of being synthesized as no roles.

AgentRole.description: Role of an agent in the system hierarchy.

oneOf.description: System-level (can do anything).
Manager agent with subordinates.
Regular agent.

AuditAppendReceipt.description:
Commit-before-ack reference for one operation audit event. An idempotent
retry returns the original sequence and hash.

`reservation_seq` is the sequence of the reservation this event belongs
to (its own, for a reservation). `outcome_seq` is the sequence of the
terminal outcome linked to that reservation, and is absent while the
reservation is still pending -- which is how a caller that was interrupted
between reserving and recording the outcome finds, by replaying its
reservation, that the outcome is still owed.

AuditEventProof.description:
One operation event bound to a verified hash chain. `chain_verified` is
false when any entry in the graph's chain fails verification.

AuditReport.description:
Outcome of walking a graph's tamper-evident hash-chained audit log
(CONCEPT:EG-KG.sharding.row-level-security, `Method::AuditVerify`). `ok` is true when every entry's stored
hash matches the recomputed chain hash AND the sequence is contiguous from 0;
`first_broken_seq` carries the position of the first detected break.

AuthMode.description: How graph-os establishes who a human caller is.

oneOf.description: Demo mode: the authenticator always answers the bootstrap principal.
Local accounts in this store.
External identity providers (with an optional local fallback).

AuthenticateOutcome.description:
How a sign-in resolved. Unknown user, wrong password and disabled
account all answer `bad`: a caller cannot enumerate accounts.

oneOf.description: A live session was opened.
Too many recent failures; retry after `retry_after_ms`.
A second factor is owed; the session is open but `mfa_pending`.
A group requires MFA and none is enrolled; no session was opened.
The password must be changed first; no session was opened.

AuthenticateResult.description: The answer to `authenticate` / `external_login` / a second factor.

DirectoryGroup.description:
A directory group (SCIM `Groups`, an LDAP group). Its membership is
authoritative: an upsert replaces it.

members.description: Principal ids; each must be linked to this IdP.

ElevationAction.description:
The graph action an elevation may grant. Deliberately NOT
`crate::acl::RbacAction`: `Admin` is unrepresentable here.

ElevationLease.description: One elevation: a control lease of kind [`RBAC_ELEVATION_KIND`].

approver_parties.description: The approver's one-way party ids, once approved.

grantee.description: The effective identity the scopes are granted to (the requester).

request_digest.description: Digest of the request as recorded; an approval must name it.

requester_parties.description: The requester's one-way party ids; an approver may share none.

revision.description: 1 at request, bumped by every transition.

scopes.description: The immutable grant body, sorted and unique.

ElevationScope.description: One granted (graph, action) pair. The graph is a literal graph name.

ElevationStatus.description: Where an elevation is in its one-way lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Waiting for a second identity's approval; grants nothing.
Approved and inside its window; grants its scopes.

Grant.description:
A grant binding a role to an (`resource`, `action`, `effect`) triple
(CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature).

GrantEffect.description: Whether a [`Grant`] permits or forbids the action (CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature).

GroupRecord.description: A group: members plus the roles every member holds.

members.description:
principal id → membership source (`local` or `<idp_id>`); an
IdP-sourced membership is recomputed at every login/sync.

mfa_required.description:
Operator ruling 2026-09-24: MFA is optional for everyone, and an
administrator may require it per group. A member of a group with this
set cannot complete a sign-in without a confirmed second factor.

actor.description: The acting principal (or `engine` for a store-internal event).

chain.description: sha256 over `prev` and every other field of this entry.

detail.description: A short, secret-free detail (an op name, a reason code).

prev.description: `chain` of the previous entry (empty for the first ever).

IdentityConfig.description: The singleton. `epoch` increments on every accepted change.

issuer_kid_current.description:
The local issuer's current signing key id, recorded at each
transition so every mode change is tied to a key rotation.

oneOf.description: A `RegisterIdentity` outside the store, recorded in its audit trail.
An `RbacAdmin` role or grant change, recorded in the store's audit trail.
A sampled authorization denial, drained into the durable audit trail.
An administrator's SQL dump was merged.
Governed changes (proposals requiring two-person approval).
Directory provisioning (SCIM / LDAP sync).
A second factor was removed (WebAuthn credential).
A signed-out user asked for a password reset (issued or not).
An administrator registered or repaired the engine's System identity.
A write that answers nothing but whether it changed state.
`export_sql`: the dump text.
`list_provisioned`.
`webauthn_credentials`.
`issue_password_reset`.

IdpConfig.description:
An identity-provider configuration. `secret_ref` names a secret in the
secrets backend; a secret value is never stored here.

config_json.description: Protocol configuration (issuer, endpoints, metadata) as a JSON object.

IdpKind.description: Which protocol an identity provider speaks.

JitPolicy.description: What happens on the first sign-in of an unlinked subject.

oneOf.description: Refuse: users are pre-provisioned by an admin, SCIM or LDAP sync.
Create a new principal on first sign-in.

Link to an existing principal with the same VERIFIED e-mail. Off by
default: cross-IdP e-mail linking is an account-takeover vector.

LedgerReadResult.description:
Materialized result of a `Method::GetLedger` call (BUG A1, 2026-08-12: `GetLedger`
returned an empty list even after real mutations had committed). The prior wire
shape was a bare `Vec<String>`, which made "the ledger is genuinely empty" and
"the ledger could not be read for this request's scope" indistinguishable — both
serialized to `[]`, so a caller (e.g. `agent_utilities.workflows.epistemic_sync`'s
`flush_ledger_to_backend`, a real production sync path) could not tell "nothing to
sync" from "I silently read nothing". Root cause: the terminal handler
unconditionally reads through the row-level-security PROJECTED core (built by
`GraphReadAuthority::project_core` / `build_projection`, which constructs its
detached copy via `add_node_no_ledger`/`add_edge_no_ledger` and therefore never
carries a ledger — see that function's own doc), even though `GetLedger` is
authorized by its own dedicated `ledger:read` RBAC action (`eg_capabilities`)
enforced upstream in `dispatch.rs` before any handler runs at all — the row
projection was a redundant SECOND gate that, instead of narrowing visibility,
destroyed the data outright. Because `security` (and therefore
`GraphReadAuthority::is_active()`) is compiled into the default `full` build,
this fired on every request in production, unconditionally.

`populated: true` means `entries` reflects the graph's REAL, authoritative
ledger (however many entries — legitimately empty when nothing has mutated
since the last flush/clear: that is a genuine `[]`, not a lie). `populated:
false` means the ledger could not be read for this request's scope; `entries`
is always empty in that case and callers MUST NOT treat it as "nothing to
sync". Any future call site that cannot certify it is reading the
authoritative (non-projected) core must answer `not_populated_for_scope()`
explicitly rather than silently returning a `populated: true` empty list —
that explicit branch is what stops this exact regression from shipping silent
a second time.

watermark.description:
BUG A1 follow-up (2026-08-12): the mutation ledger is a purely
IN-MEMORY, capped ring (100k entries, drop-oldest-half — see
`GraphTxn::push_ledger` in `eg_core::graph`) — NOT a durable change
log. A cold-tenant idle
offload/hibernate cycle, `MAX_RESIDENT_GRAPHS` eviction + lazy
rehydrate, a process restart, or simply exceeding the cap can all
empty or truncate `entries` while the underlying mutations remain
fully durable in redb — a typed `populated: true` alone does not
prove `entries` is COMPLETE. `watermark`
(`GraphCore::ledger_watermark`) is the 0-based sequence of the
OLDEST entry `entries` can vouch for: `0` on a graph that has never
dropped anything (from THIS in-memory instance's point of view); a
caller that tracks watermark across reads can detect it advancing
(or a previously-nonzero watermark resetting to a lower value after
an eviction/restart) as proof that history was silently dropped,
rather than inferring completeness from `entries` merely being
nonzero.

LocalFallback.description: Which local credentials still sign in while the mode is `external`.

oneOf.description: Administrators only (the break-glass account).

MappingRule.description:
One ordered claim → role/group mapping rule. The target is `role:<id>` or
`group:<id>`; a rule reaching an approver- or admin-class scope must be
marked `privileged`.

MerkleInclusionReport.description:
Result of `Method::AuditProveInclusion` (provenance anchoring, CONCEPT:EG-KG.sharding.row-level-security): a
Merkle inclusion proof for one node against a prior provenance anchor,
ALREADY VERIFIED server-side. `verified` is the tamper signal: `false`
whenever the node's CURRENT durable content does not re-hash to the leaf
folded into `anchored_root_sha256` at anchor time — including when the node
was altered by an otherwise-ordinary later write, not just raw byte-level
tampering. `included == false` only means `node_id` was never part of that
anchor's window (a different anchor, a non-provenance node, or a node created
after this anchor ran) — not itself evidence of tampering.

MerkleProofStep.description:
One Merkle audit-path step, wire-encoded: a hex-encoded sibling subtree hash
plus which side it sits on. See [`MerkleInclusionReport`].

MerkleSide.description:
Which side of its parent a Merkle audit-path sibling sits on (provenance
anchoring, CONCEPT:EG-KG.sharding.row-level-security). The verifier folds the running hash with each
step's sibling on the side named here — RFC 6962 §2.1.1 Merkle audit path
semantics.

PrincipalResolution.description: What the local issuer puts in a principal's token.

mfa_required.description: A group this principal belongs to requires a second factor.

scopes.description: Registered scopes only; an unregistered scope on a role is dropped.

session_mfa_pending.description: Set by `resolve_session`: the session still owes its second factor.

ProvisionedUser.description: One linked subject and its principal.

RbacAction.description: An action a grant permits or denies over a resource (CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature).

RbacGrantRemoval.description: `RbacAdmin` op `RemoveGrant`: whether the grant was present.

RbacPolicyListing.description: `RbacAdmin` op `List`: the whole current RBAC policy.

oneOf.description: Operator ruling 2026-09-24: the default.

ResetDelivery.description: Where a self-service reset link goes (`None`: nowhere, uniformly).

ResourceSelector.description:
What a [`Grant`] applies to (CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature). Ordered by [`specificity`] so the
evaluator can implement "most-specific-resource wins": a named graph beats a
label, which beats a glob pattern, which beats "all".

[`specificity`]: ResourceSelector::specificity

oneOf.description: Every resource (least specific).

A glob over the graph name — a single optional leading and/or trailing `*`
wildcard (e.g. `agent:*`, `*:private`, `*log*`).
A node label.
One named graph (most specific).

Role.description:
A durable RBAC role with an optional set of parent roles forming a hierarchy
(CONCEPT:EG-KG.compute.feature). A role transitively inherits every grant of its parents.

RoleGraphGrant.description:
One graph grant of a role, projected into the RBAC image under the role
`idm:<role_id>`.

RoleRecord.description:
A role: a named set of registry scopes plus graph grants projected into
the RBAC image as role `idm:<role_id>`.

SessionView.description:
A session without its id or id hash. `handle` is a short, one-way
prefix an operator can use to tell sessions apart.

UserKind.description: Whether a principal is a person or a workload.

UserStatus.description:
A principal's lifecycle state. Nothing is ever deleted: a deprovisioned
principal keeps its id, links and owned data, and holds no authority.

oneOf.description:
Must set a new password (admin reset, or local mode entered without a
credential) before any session is issued.

is_bootstrap.description: Whether this is the engine's built-in bootstrap principal.

principal_id.description: The store's stable key (never the mutable, normalized `username`).

WebauthnCredentialView.description: A WebAuthn credential as the broker needs it to verify an assertion.
